# Objetivos del archivo:

1.Crear S4 R data object, en este caso llamado phyloseq, desde la tabla `asv_table`, `tax_table`, y metadata.Unificando todo en un solo objeto de datos. 
2. Remove any ASVs that are **cloroplasts**
3. Remove ASVs that are **mitochondria**
4. Check for **reverse complements**
5. Check los **sequencing depth** 

## Input
1. **Raw phyloseq object**: `data/its/02_AssignASVs/raw_phyloseq.RData`
2. `asv_table` 
3. `tax_table`
3. `Metadata`

## Output
1. A clean phyloseq object (S4 object): `data/03_PreProcessing/clean_physeq.RData`

# Load Data

```{r load-data}
# Load ASV table
ASV_table <- read_tsv("data/its/02_Assign_ASVs/ASV_table.tsv") %>%
  column_to_rownames(var = colnames(.)[1]) # Toma la primera columna y la hace rownames
# Lo mismo para la tabla de taxonomía
ASV_tax_table <- read_tsv("data/its/02_Assign_ASVs/ASV_taxonomy.tsv") %>%
  column_to_rownames(var = colnames(.)[1])
# Load la tabla de conteos
track_counts_df <- readRDS("data/its/02_Assign_ASVs/track_counts_df.rds")

# Estandarizar los nombres de las muestras
track_counts_df$sample_names <- sapply(strsplit(track_counts_df$sample_names, "_"), '[', 1)
# Como se ve después? 
head(track_counts_df)

# Importar la tabla de promedios de calidad de agua
agua_df <- read_csv("data/its/metadata/agua_promedios.csv", col_names = TRUE) %>%
  clean_names()
# Ensamblar la metadata  
metadata_fixed <-read_csv("data/its/metadata/metadata.csv", col_names = TRUE) %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  # Renombrar la columna de codigo para que sea sample_names
  dplyr::rename(sample_names = codigo) %>%
  
  # Elimina las filas vacias
  drop_na(sample_names) %>%
  
  # Eliminar filas que tengan guiones bajos pero no codigo de muestra
  filter(!str_detect(sample_names, "^_+$|^-+$")) %>%
  
  # Estandarizar el nombre de las muestras
  mutate(sample_names = str_replace_all(sample_names, " ", "-")) %>%
  mutate(sample_names = str_trim(sample_names)) %>%
  # Inyectar las calidades promedio de agua por localidad
  left_join(agua_df, by = "localidad") %>%
  
  # Inner_join para ignorar las cosas no secuenciadas y añadir stats DADA2
  inner_join(track_counts_df, by = "sample_names") %>%
  
  # Prueba de sanidad para que solo haya un registro por muestra
  distinct(sample_names, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  
  # Phyloseq exige que los identificadores de muestra estén asignados como 'rownames' 
  # para poder ensamblar el objeto S4. Sin embargo, las herramientas de Tidyverse 
  # (como dplyr y ggplot2) operan sobre columnas explícitas y no leen los rownames.
  # Como la función 'column_to_rownames' consume (elimina) la columna que se le pasa, 
  # creamos una copia temporal para sacrificarla en este paso. Esto satisface el 
  # requisito de Phyloseq y conserva la columna original 'sample_names' intacta 
  # para uso futuro en tidyverse y facil acceso a la metadata
  mutate(rownames_temp = sample_names) %>% 
  column_to_rownames(var = "rownames_temp")
# Verificar dimensiones finales
dim(metadata_fixed)
```

# Create a phyloseq object!

## Creacion de objeto phyloseq 

```{r phyloseq-handoff}
raw_physeq <-
  phyloseq::phyloseq(otu_table(ASV_table, taxa_are_rows = TRUE),
         sample_data(metadata_fixed),
         tax_table(as.matrix(ASV_tax_table)))

raw_physeq
```


## Remover todo lo no_fungi
```{r rm-!fungi}
# Mantener estrictamente solo a los ASVs asignados al reino Fungi
fungi_physeq <-
  raw_physeq %>%
  subset_taxa(Kingdom == "k__Fungi")

# How many ASVs were non-fungi (e.g., host DNA, plants, protists)?
numNonFungi_ASVs <- ntaxa(raw_physeq) - ntaxa(fungi_physeq)

numNonFungi_ASVs

# Eliminar secuencias que no tienen asignacion a nivel de phylum 
clean_physeq <-
  fungi_physeq %>%
  subset_taxa(!is.na(Phylum))

# How many ambiguous ASVs were removed?
numAmbiguous_ASVs <- ntaxa(fungi_physeq) - ntaxa(clean_physeq)
numAmbiguous_ASVs
```

## Buscar complemento reverso
```{r reverse-complements}
# Pull out Taxa Table
tax_table <- 
  clean_physeq %>%
  tax_table() %>% 
  data.frame()

# Grab ASV Sequences and Names
asv_names <- tax_table$ASV
asv_seqs <- tax_table$ASVseqs

# Create empty comparison matrix
asv_rev_comp <- matrix(nrow=length(asv_seqs), ncol = length(asv_seqs)) 

# Fix the names in the rows and columns 
rownames(asv_rev_comp) <- asv_names
colnames(asv_rev_comp) <- asv_names

# Convert sequences to Biostrings
asv_dna <- DNAStringSet(asv_seqs) 

# Inspect 
head(asv_dna)

# Construct reverse complement
asv_rev_dna <- reverseComplement(asv_dna) 

# Now loop through every asv sequence to check 
for(i in 1:length(asv_seqs)){ # For each asv sequence...
  match_vec <- asv_dna[i] == asv_rev_dna # Compare it to the reverse complement of every other sequence...
  asv_rev_comp[,i] <- match_vec # Write that logical vector as a new column 
}

# Find how many TRUEs (matches) we have, divide by 2 because each pair occurs twice
cat("For", sum(asv_rev_comp) / 2,"ASVs, the reverse complement will need to be removed") 

# The current data objec
clean_physeq
```

# Asesorar la profundidad del resto de las muestras

```{r read-depth, fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
# El objeto actual
clean_physeq

# Make a metadata_df for joining
metadata_df <- 
  clean_physeq %>%
  sample_data() %>% 
  data.frame()

# What is the library size/sequencing depth for each sample? 
seqSums_df <- 
  clean_physeq %>%
  otu_table() %>%
  # Sum each sample column 
  colSums() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "sample_names") %>%
  left_join(., metadata_df, by = "sample_names")

# Rename second column 
colnames(seqSums_df)[2] <- "TotalSeqs"

# check
dim(seqSums_df)
head(seqSums_df)

# Show the depth of samples 
seqSums_df %>%
  dplyr::select(sample_names, TotalSeqs) %>%
  arrange(TotalSeqs) %>%
  head()

# plot it as a bar plot 
numSeq_bar_plot <-
seqSums_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=reorder(sample_names, TotalSeqs), y = TotalSeqs,
             fill = localidad)) + 
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = localidad_colors) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank()) + 
  labs(y = "Read Depth", x = "Sample")

# histogram
numSeq_hist_plot <- 
  seqSums_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x= TotalSeqs, fill = localidad)) + 
  geom_histogram(color = "black") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = localidad_colors) +
  labs(y = "# of Samples", x = "Read Depth") + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# Density plot 
numSeq_density_plot <-
seqSums_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(TotalSeqs, fill = localidad)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = localidad_colors) +
  labs(x = "Read Depth")


# Put it all together 
numSeq_bar_plot + numSeq_hist_plot + numSeq_density_plot + 
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") 

# What's the min seq depth? 
min(sample_sums(clean_physeq))

# Final check of the sequencing depth for now
seqSums_df %>%
  dplyr::select(sample_names, TotalSeqs) %>%
  arrange(TotalSeqs)
```
